'''Global Health Limited''', [[Trade name|d/b/a]] '''Medanta''',  is an Indian [[For-profit hospital|for-profit]] [[Private hospital|private]] [[hospital network]] based in [[Gurgaon]]. The chain was started in 2009 by [[cardiac surgeon]] [[Naresh Trehan]] and Sunil Sachdeva.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/gurgaon/Gurgaon-hospital-scores-a-first-with-robotic-surgery/articleshow/6957111.cms |title=Gurgaon hospital scores a first with robotic surgery |website=Times of India |date=20 November 2010 |access-date=2 February 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130629134229/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-11-20/gurgaon/28263024_1_robotic-surgery-robotic-procedures-cardiac-surgery |archive-date=29 June 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Dash |first1=Jayajit |title=Medanta may invest Rs 750-1,000 cr on high-end hospital in Odisha |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/medanta-may-invest-rs-750-1-000-cr-on-high-end-hospital-in-odisha-117020400631_1.html |access-date=3 November 2022 |work=Business Standard |date=4 February 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sonavane |first=Ravindra N. |date=2021-09-30 |title=Medanta hospital chain files for share sale |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/ipo/naresh-trehan-s-medanta-files-drhp-with-sebi-for-ipo-11632987207735.html |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref>

==History==
In 2004, cardiac surgeon [[Naresh Trehan]] began working on Medanta, along with Sunil Sachdeva, after leaving [[Fortis Healthcare|Escorts Heart Institute]]. In June 2006, [[Avenue Capital Group]] invested {{INRconvert|224|c|year=2006|mode=historical}} in the venture.<ref name="carlyle">{{cite news |title=Carlyle Group picks 27% in Medanta Medicity Hospital for Rs 960 cr |url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/carlyle-group-picks-27--in-medanta-medicity-hospital-for-rs-960-cr/1209306/0 |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=Indian Express}}</ref>

In 2009, Medanta launched its first hospital, Medanta - The Medicity in [[Gurgaon]], a 1250-bed [[super-specialty hospital]] spread over 43 acres which was built at a cost of about {{INRconvert|1200|c|mode=historical|year=2009}}.<ref name=fin>{{cite news |title=Magic of Medanta |url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/magic-of-medanta/648319/0 |publisher=Financial Express |date=19 July 2010 |accessdate=23 April 2013|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100725093557/https://www.financialexpress.com/news/magic-of-medanta/648319/0|archive-date=25 July 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Medanta has no effect on competitors|url=http://www.sify.com/finance/medanta-has-no-effect-on-competitors-news-news-kdlcbbjadec.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307081702/http://www.sify.com/finance/medanta-has-no-effect-on-competitors-news-news-kdlcbbjadec.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 March 2014 |date= 11 March 2010 |website=[[Sify]] |accessdate=23 April 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Bhattacharjee |first1=Arindam |title=Operation Medanta |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/operation-medanta-110071900068_1.html |access-date=3 November 2022 |work=Business Standard |date=19 July 2010}}</ref>

In 2013, private equity firm [[The Carlyle Group|Carlyle Group]] acquired Avenue Capital Group's 27% stake in Medanta for {{INRconvert|960|c|year=2013|mode=historical}}, valuing the company at {{INRconvert|3550|c|year=2013|mode=historical}}.<ref name="carlyle"/> In 2015, [[Singapore]]-based [[Temasek Holdings]] purchased [[Punj Lloyd]]'s 17.74% stake in the company.<ref>{{cite news |title=Temasek buys 18% stake in Medanta from Punj Lloyd |url=https://www.vccircle.com/temasek-buys-18-stake-medanta-punj-lloyd |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=VCCircle}}</ref>

In 2015, Medanta launched a 160-bed hospital in [[Indore]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr Naresh Trehan inaugurates Medanta — The Medicity in Indore |url=https://health.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/hospitals/dr-naresh-trehan-inaugurates-medanta-the-medicity-in-indore/46231992 |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=Economic Times |language=en}}</ref> Later that year, Medanta acquired the Abdur Razzaque Ansari Memorial Weavers' Hospital on the outskirts of [[Ranchi]] from [[Apollo Hospitals]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Medanta forays into Irba heal hub with promise of better care |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/jharkhand/medanta-forays-into-irba-heal-hub-with-promise-of-better-care/cid/1430790 |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=Telegraph India}}</ref>

In 2018, Medanta opened a 200-bed hospital in [[Sri Ganganagar]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Medanta opens 200-bed hospital at Sri Ganganagar |url=http://www.uniindia.com/medanta-opens-200-bed-hospital-at-sri-ganganagar/states/news/1222699.html |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=United News of India}}</ref> In 2019, Medanta began operations of a 1000-bed, multi-specialty hospital in [[Lucknow]] called Medanta Avadh,<ref>{{cite news |title=CM inaugurates 1,000-bed Medanta hosp in Lucknow |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/cm-inaugurates-1-000-bed-medanta-hosp-in-lucknow/story-R38MWMl7ylBaE95xI0covM.html |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=Hindustan Times |date=5 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref> which was constructed at a cost of {{INRconvert|1000|c|mode=historical|year=2015}}.<ref>{{cite news |title=Construction of Medanta hospital in Lucknow begins |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ians/construction-of-medanta-hospital-in-lucknow-begins-115101501498_1.html |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=Business Standard |date=15 October 2015}}</ref> In 2019, it was reported that [[Manipal Hospitals India|Manipal Hospitals]] had agreed to acquire Medanta for {{INRconvert|5800|c|mode=historical|year=2019}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/manipal-hotells-to-buy-medanta-in-rs-5800-crore-deal/articleshow/69509728.cms|title=Manipal Hospitals to buy Medanta in Rs 5,800 crore deal|last1=Balakrishnan|first1=Reghu|date=2019-05-27|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-10-03|last2=PM|first2=Indulal}}</ref> However, the deal was called off later that year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rs 5,800 cr Medanta-Manipal deal falls through as sides disagree over valuation |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/manipal-medanta-talks-fail-disagreement-overvaluation-led-deal-demise-221847-2019-08-17 |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=Business Today |date=17 August 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, Medanta inaugurated the 500-bed Jay Prabha Medanta Super Specialty Hospital in [[Patna]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Patna: CM Nitish Kumar inaugurates 500-bed Medanta hospital |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/cm-to-open-500-bed-medanta-hospital-today/articleshow/87376052.cms |access-date=13 November 2022 |work=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref> In November 2022, Medanta launched its [[initial public offering]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Medanta hospital chain IPO to open on November 3 |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/ipo/medanta-hospital-chain-ipo-to-open-on-november-3-9391451.html |access-date=3 November 2022 |work=Moneycontrol |language=en}}</ref>

* Medanta-The Medicity: 2nd rank, Best All India Multi Speciality Hospital Ranking 2022 by [[Outlook (Indian magazine)]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-20 |title=Best All India Multi Speciality Hospital Ranking 2022 Presented By Outlook & NEB Research |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/outlook-spotlight/best-all-india-multi-speciality-hospital-ranking-2022-presented-by-outlook-neb-research-news-192310 |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=[[Outlook (Indian magazine)]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Hospitals ==

Medanta Group has following hospitals :

* Medanta Abdur Razzaque Ansari Memorial Weavers’ Hospital, [[Ranchi]]

== Controversies ==
In 2012, a donor died during the [[liver transplantation]] operation despite the fact that a pre-operation medical report clearly stated that donor's liver "was not ideal for donation."<ref>{{Cite web |agency=TNN|date=Jul 3, 2012 |title=Dead donor's kin demand justice {{!}} Gurgaon News - Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/gurgaon/dead-donors-kin-demand-justice/articleshow/14618372.cms |access-date=2023-01-02 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref>

In April 2013, the former [[Chief Justice of India]] [[J. S. Verma]] died from multiple organ failure at Medanta-The Medicity Hospital. The family of Jurist Verma alleged that he died due to medical negligence.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-10-07 |title=Was Justice JS Verma's death a case of medical negligence?  |url=https://www.firstpost.com/india/was-justice-js-vermas-death-a-case-of-medical-negligence-1157265.html |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=Firstpost |language=en}}</ref> Later, in 2014, the hospital and its team of doctors got the clean chit from the [[Delhi Medical Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nanda Jha |first=Durgesh |date=July 23, 2014 |title=DMC rules out negligence in ex-CJI's death |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/dmc-rules-out-negligence-in-ex-cjis-death/articleshow/38882150.cms |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref>

In 2014, a Junior doctor employed at Medanta Medicity in Gurgaon was apprehended on allegations of sexual assault and harassment against his sister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Siddhartha |date=2014-04-27 |title=Gurgaon doctor held on charges of raping, molesting his sister |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/gurgaon-doctor-held-on-charges-of-raping-molesting-his-sister/ |access-date=2023-10-27 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

In 2018, a report was published in [[The Wire (India)]] where it mentioned the role of India's [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare]] took an arbitrary step and brokered a deal between the kin of a deceased boy who died in the Medanta hospital during treatment.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-03-29 |title=Father withdraws complaint, Medanta refunds ₹15 lakh |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/father-withdraws-complaint-medanta-refunds-15-lakh/article23386460.ece |access-date=2022-11-06 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> The hospital was initially accused of overcharging and medical negligence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhuyan |first=Anoo |title=Health Ministry Brokers Rs 15 Lakh Refund to Bereaved Parents, Medanta Uses It as Hush-Money |url=https://thewire.in/health/health-ministry-brokers-a-refund-of-rs-15-lakh-to-bereaved-parents-medanta-uses-it-as-hush-money |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=The Wire}}</ref> The reporter on this case writes, "Medanta used the opportunity to hush Gopendra (deceased boy's father) up completely and kill his criminal complaint against them. For now and in this case, the hospital appears to have succeeded."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhuyan |first=Anoo |title=Two Fathers Fighting Big Hospitals For Justice – But On Different Paths |url=https://thewire.in/health/two-bereaved-fathers-fighting-big-hospitals-for-justice-but-on-very-different-paths |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=The Wire}}</ref>

In 2019, the [[Government of Jharkhand]] issued a directive to take legal action against the Medanta Abdur Razzaque Ansari Memorial Weavers' Hospital in [[Ranchi]] for a suspected instance of [[Medical malpractice|medical negligence]] involving a kidney transplant; the doctors did not filter the blood before the transplant, thus the operation failed. When the public petition was being heard, the patient's relatives brought forward an allegation that the doctor who operated was putting pressure on them to retract the [[first information report]] they had filed against him at the [[Ormanjhi]] police station.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Neglect whip on Medanta hospital |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/jharkhand/neglect-whip-on-medanta-hospital/cid/1691793 |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=www.telegraphindia.com}}</ref>

In 2019, [[Madhya Pradesh High Court]] fined the Indore unit of the hospital {{INRconvert|25|l|year=2019|mode=historical}}, for failing to establish an internal complaints committee as required by Section 4(1) of the [[Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Saxena |first=Akshita |date=2019-09-18 |title=Sexual Harassment At Workplace: Hospital Fined 25 Lakh For Not Having ICC |url=https://www.livelaw.in/news-updates/sexual-harassment-at-workplace-148214 |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=www.livelaw.in |language=en}}</ref>

In June 2020, the [[Enforcement Directorate]] filed a [[money laundering]] case against the hospital, its chairman [[Naresh Trehan]], Atul Punj and unidentified Haryana government officials for suspected irregularities in the hospital's 2004 land allocation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ED Files PMLA Case Against Dr Naresh Trehan, Medanta Hospital |url=https://thewire.in/government/naresh-trehan-cardiologist-medanta-pmla |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=The Wire}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tiwary |first=Deeptiman |date=2020-06-11 |title=ED files money laundering case against Medanta |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/delhi/ed-files-money-laundering-case-against-medanta-6453133/ |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, the [[District Collector]] of [[Indore]] ordered the closure of Indore's Medanta hospital-owned pharmacy store because "the hospital was not providing any information" to the [[Madhya Pradesh|state]]'s Chief Medical Health Officer (CMHO). Earlier, an inquiry was initiated against an overcharging case by the same officer, but the hospital administration "did not pay heed to it."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indore collector orders closure of Medanta hospital pharma shop |url=https://www.dailypioneer.com/2021/state-editions/indore-collector-orders-closure-of-medanta-hospital-pharma-shop.html |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=The Pioneer |language=en}}</ref>

== Accidents ==
In 2017, an air ambulance from Medanta Hospital en route to [[Bangkok]] was involved in a crash landing at [[Nakhon Phanom Airport]], about 730 kilometers from the Thai capital, resulting in the pilot's death and injuring two medical professionals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Medanta Hospital's air ambulance crashes near Bangkok, pilot dead, 2 doctors in ICU |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/air-ambulance-medanta-hospital-crash-bangkok-964256-2017-03-06 |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=India Today |date=6 March 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Scroll Staff |title=Pilot killed as air ambulance of Gurgaon's Medanta Hospital crash lands in Thailand |url=https://scroll.in/latest/831074/pilot-killed-as-air-ambulance-of-gurgaons-medanta-hospital-crash-lands-in-thailand |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=Scroll.in |date=7 March 2017 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2022, a fire broke out in the [[intensive care unit]] of Medanta's Indore hospital. However, there were no reports of any casualties.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-16 |title=Fire breaks out in ICU of private hospital in Indore; patients safe |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/national/north-and-central/fire-breaks-out-in-icu-of-private-hospital-in-indore-patients-safe-1071747.html |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> The hospital's fire alarm system did not appear operational, as the eyewitness stated.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Antriksh |last=Singh|date=January 17, 2022 |title=Close shave for patients after fire at Medanta hospital in Indore |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/indore/close-shave-for-patients-in-fire-at-medanta-hospital-in-indore/articleshow/88948034.cms |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref>

extract: Global Health Limited, d/b/a Medanta,  is an Indian for-profit private hospital network based in Gurgaon. The chain was started in 2009 by cardiac surgeon Naresh Trehan and Sunil Sachdeva.
